claim: Adding 2 x (RL-Math - base) to Think-SFT turns the abstaining cap-hit companions of a lone right sample into finished wrong answers, so on problems with exactly 1 right of 3 samples the M(2) vote is right at least 0.15 less often than Think-SFT's.
measured: D = VR_ThinkSFT - VR_M2 = 0.19 [0.08, 0.30] (0.82 vs 0.63), n 41 / 32 lone-right problems (< 50), null D_null -0.02 [-0.11, 0.08]; threshold 0.15; ~240-300 lone-right per arm (~3,400 problems) would decide
